Secured Bail Help in Delaware

Secured bail means money, property, or another form of security may be required before release. Families should confirm the court order and understand financial responsibility before moving forward.

Secured bail can be confusing because it may involve cash, property, a bail bond, or someone posting security on the defendant's behalf. The exact next step depends on what the Delaware court ordered.

This page focuses on secured bail in Delaware. It should not compete with felony, misdemeanor, payment plan, or county location pages.

What secured bail usually means

Delaware Courts explain that secured bail requires the defendant to pay the court a designated amount of money or post security in the amount of bail before release. That security may be posted by the defendant or someone else, including a relative or bail bondsman.

When secured bail is different from other bond pages

This page is about the bond type, not the criminal charge. If the issue is a felony charge, use the felony bonds page. If the issue is a misdemeanor charge, use the misdemeanor bonds page. If the court order says unsecured or cash-only, those release types work differently from secured bail.

Local secured bail questions in Delaware

In New Castle County, Wilmington, Newark, and nearby Delaware communities, families often hear the words secured, cash-only, or unsecured and do not know which one applies. The safest first step is to read the written bond order and confirm the exact wording before arranging payment or signing.

What families should confirm first

  • Exact bail amount
  • Whether the order says secured bail or cash-only
  • Who can post security
  • Whether collateral or a co-signer may be required
  • What written agreement will be signed

Questions before using secured bail help

  • What is due now?
  • What is refundable and what is not?
  • What happens if court is missed?
  • What documents and receipts will be provided?
  • Who is financially responsible?

Secured Bail FAQs

Can a bail bondsman help with secured bail in Delaware?

In some secured bail situations, a bail bond agent may be able to help. Cash-only, unsecured, and own-recognizance release work differently, so confirm the exact bond type first. If the order says unsecured, read our unsecured bail guide before assuming money is due upfront.

Is secured bail the same as cash-only bail?

No. Secured bail and cash-only bail are different release types. Families should read the court order carefully before assuming a standard bail bond can be used.

What should I ask before posting secured bail?

Ask about the full bail amount, security required, premium or payment arrangement, collateral, co-signer responsibility, receipts, and missed-court consequences.
